author: Gene Holcombe
text:
It can be due to compression.  Normally when a sensor is compressed, by laying on it, it causes the filament to move out of the interstitial fluid.  Then returns to normal after compression.  Sometimes if you compress too hard it permanently compresses and will show bad/low results for all readings.  It’s best to be safe and don’t lean on or lay on your sensor.  It’s sensitive.  
If you’re on Mounjaro you will experience lower lows than you are used to.  Sometimes it will drop very low quickly and over shoot.  This usually happened to me at night or if I ate something sweet.  Mounjaro responds quickly to anything sugary by causing your body to release insulin quickly to compensate for the sugar.
